title: Collatz structured cases and stopping-time growth

problemStatement.formal: T(n)=\begin{cases}n/2&2\mid n\\3n+1&2\nmid n\end{cases},\quad \operatorname{ReachesOne}(n):=\exists k, T^k(n)=1,\quad S(N)=\frac1N\sum_{n\le N}\sigma(n).
problemStatement.plain: Study structured Collatz inputs, bounded cycle obstructions, and average stopping-time growth while keeping the full conjecture explicit as open. The Lean files prove powers-of-two and small-value cases, period-4 and halving-bound constraints, and stopping-time definitions, with deep global claims recorded as axioms.
whyMatters: Structured Collatz families are a practical formalization target short of the full unsolved conjecture.
Small-cycle exclusions expose the arithmetic constraints behind parity-pattern approaches.
Average stopping-time growth connects computable Collatz dynamics with analytic number-theory heuristics.

proven: `pow_two_reaches_one` proves that powers of two reach one under Collatz iteration.
`no_j1_period4_cycle` rules out a one-odd-step period-4 cycle under the stated parity hypotheses.
`min_halvings_five_odd` and its siblings give explicit halving lower bounds for five through eight odd steps.
`stoppingTime_one` and `stoppingTime_two` verify base stopping-time values in the average-stopping-time framework.
open: The full Collatz conjecture, a closed form for Mersenne-like stopping times, and the asymptotic growth of average stopping time remain open.
The declared Lean files intentionally use axioms for global external claims such as the full conjecture, Eliahou's cycle bound, and Terras density.
knownResults.goal: Separate the proved structured Collatz cases from axiom-backed global theory so future work can safely target one bounded family or analytic claim at a time.
